sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r7/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (in memory via openpyxl read_only + zipfile): 'Quality Checks' row 13 (#12, block 'B - task.toml & run wiring', no_prebuilt_image_shadows_the_agent_dockerfile, "[environment].docker_image isn't set while the agent Dockerfile still has active build steps (which would skip the Dockerfile entirely)."); 'Internal Quality Checks' row 13 (same check, "...(which would skip it entirely).", no extra annotation column); drawings1-4 contain no text; no comments/threadedComments parts present
grep -rni 'docker_image|image *=' over the whole frozen task/ tree (no matches, rc=1); toml files enumerated: task.toml, tests/scoring.toml, 5 judge.toml
evidence: Frozen task/task.toml [environment] (lines 20-24) contains only build_timeout_sec = 600.0, network_mode = "public", cpus = 2, memory_mb = 4096; there is no docker_image key anywhere in the file or in any other file of the frozen task tree (recursive grep for 'docker_image' and 'image =' returned no match). [verifier.environment] (lines 37-38) holds only network_mode = "public". The agent Dockerfile task/environment/Dockerfile has active build steps (FROM node:22-bookworm-slim; RUN apt-get install ca-certificates git procps sqlite3; RUN npm install -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1; COPY instructions/ /instructions/; COPY assets/ /assets/; RUN chmod/git init of /app; WORKDIR /app; CMD sleep infinity), so those steps are live and nothing shadows them. Both task.toml and the Dockerfile match the frozen template byte-for-byte in these sections (template task.toml lines 20-24 and template environment/Dockerfile lines 1-26 are identical apart from the task-specific [task]/[metadata] values), consistent with staged-task-contract.md:78 and quality-checks.md:54. Counter-scenario considered: a variant that set [environment].docker_image = "<prebuilt>" would skip the COPY of /instructions and /assets that instruction.md relies on and would fail this row; the frozen candidate does not do that. No conforming alternative can fail on this row since it is purely a configuration property of the task, not of the submission. This is a static configuration check; no build or runtime evidence is required to establish the absence of the key, and no Docker build was run by this reviewer (whether the Dockerfile actually builds is row 15's concern, not this row's).
